proposals.evidence: Turner explicitly cites older Dameli žu- eat in section 2 of yuvátē, with Kati yū-, Waigali yā-, Pashai žū-/žē- and Gawarbati žu-. Perder gives modern ži/žin, infinitive žen and causative žuw/žuwaai feed, supporting membership in the same eating family while leaving the vowel alternation to explain. Use 10507 only as the existing comparative-family index for its second sense, not as a claim that the verb means yoke. The competing deeper reconstruction involving a graze/eat root, rather than the yoke root, remains open; likewise Nuristani comparison does not identify a borrowing direction.

approval: User: approve all; prefer Pashto where best matched, then Urdu for broadly Perso-Arabic terms. Approval includes qualified analyses, not a claim that uncertainties are resolved.
donor_policy: Prefer an attested Pashto donor where form and meaning fit best; otherwise prefer Urdu for broadly shared Perso-Arabic loans. Preserve explicit source attribution, phonological uncertainty and possible Nuristani mediation. Do not substitute a different dialect merely because its node is linkable.
